findings.title: Public findMany API removed without caller migration
findings.body: InsightsBookingService previously exposed findMany(findManyArgs) that applied authorization plus filter conditions through the Prisma client. This PR deletes that method and replaces it with getBaseConditions() returning a Prisma.Sql fragment for manual $queryRaw use. Any existing production caller that still calls service.findMany() will throw TypeError at runtime and break insights endpoints. The PR itself proves the contract was in use because the integration test had to be rewritten from findMany to $queryRaw. Keep a findMany-compatible wrapper or update all production call sites atomically in the same PR.

findings.title: Auth/filter fragments with top-level OR are unsafe to compose
findings.body: buildFilterConditions returns bare SQL like ("eventTypeId" = X) OR ("eventParentId" = X) with no outer parentheses, and buildOrgAuthorizationCondition/buildTeamAuthorizationCondition return (... AND ...) OR (... AND ...) with no outer parentheses. getBaseConditions happens to wrap them as (auth) AND (filter), but getAuthorizationConditions and getFilterConditions are public and return the unwrapped OR fragments. A caller that writes WHERE ${fragment} AND <other> without adding its own parentheses gets AND-binds-tighter-than-OR semantics, e.g. A OR B AND C becomes A OR (B AND C), returning rows that should have been filtered out. That is an authorization/filter bypass and data leak. Parenthesize each fragment at construction time.

findings.title: Org scope test asserts exact ANY array order from unordered queries
findings.body: The org-scope test uses toEqual against Prisma.sql containing teamIds [org.id, team.id, team2.id, team3.id] and userIds [user.id, user2.id, user3.id]. The service builds those arrays from TeamRepository.findAllByParentId and MembershipRepository.findAllByTeamIds with no ORDER BY, so database return order is undefined. SQL ANY is order-insensitive, but toEqual on Prisma.Sql values is order-sensitive, so the test can fail intermittently even when logic is correct and enforces an irrelevant ordering. Sort arrays or compare as sets.

findings.title: Caching and empty-membership/invalid-team paths no longer tested
findings.body: This PR deletes the Caching describe block while the service still caches Prisma.Sql auth/filter fragments, so stale-cache or shared-mutable-fragment regressions are now undetected. It also adds no coverage for the single-clause branches: team with zero members, org with no child teams or no members, and teamId not in org returning 1=0. Those branches change SQL shape from OR to a single AND clause and are the exact place where an empty ANY array would produce wrong or invalid SQL. Restore caching tests for Sql and add edge-case tests.
